basics.name: Divyanshu Pabia
basics.label: Systems Engineer · AI Systems at Scale
basics.summary: I am focused on understanding and improving the systems that run modern AI models, from GPU kernels and memory behavior to compilers, inference runtimes, and distributed execution. I enjoy reading systems code, profiling bottlenecks, and building experiments that turn performance questions into measurable results. My background spans backend engineering, iOS development, and network-monitoring software for Tor, and I am now specializing in AI systems, GPU computing, and efficient LLM inference.

work.name: The Tor Project
highlights: Contributed to reimplementing the Java Tor Metrics Library in Rust to retrieve, parse, and validate network descriptors from CollecTor, focusing on memory safety and extensible parsing.
Worked on a unified descriptor pipeline using object storage, a dedicated parser service, and PostgreSQL and VictoriaMetrics exports to support historical and real-time network analysis.

work.name: Infosys
highlights: Built a Hospital Management System with a Swift iOS client and Java/Spring Boot REST APIs for staff management, bookings, and real-time updates. Implemented JWT authentication and role-based access.
Containerized backend services with Docker and supported test/staging CI/CD. Strengthened API design, OpenAPI documentation, and verification through JUnit 5 and integration tests.

work.name: iOS App Development Centre
work.position: Apple and Infosys iOS App Development Program
highlights: Built Gamergrid through the Apple and Infosys program, integrating esports events, scores, and news into a Swift iOS app. Developed practical skills in URLSession, Combine, REST API integration, pagination, and resilient data fetching.

work.name: Tech Analogy
highlights: Built an expense-management backend with Spring Boot and Hibernate, using Kafka and RabbitMQ for asynchronous communication. Gained hands-on experience in transaction processing, microservices, and event-driven design.

projects.name: GeoGPT-RAG
projects.summary: Developed a geospatial assistant prototype combining retrieval over reference material, language-model interaction, and GIS tooling. Explored how to connect natural-language requests with spatial data and tools while keeping analysis steps inspectable.

projects.name: Linux virtual LIFO device
projects.summary: Implemented a virtual last-in, first-out character device as a loadable Linux kernel module. Worked with module and device interfaces, device-state management, and the user/kernel boundary to understand how applications interact with kernel-backed services.

projects.name: ARM microarchitecture in VHDL
projects.summary: Built a VHDL microarchitecture that executes a subset of ARM instructions, connecting instruction decoding, datapath behavior, and control logic. Developed a practical understanding of how instruction semantics map to hardware execution.

projects.name: Gamergrid
projects.summary: Built a native Swift app for following esports events, live scores, match statistics, and personalized news. Integrated third-party REST APIs using URLSession and Combine, with attention to pagination, resilient networking, and a responsive mobile interface.
